## Analysis
sol_0039 shows that stochastic 3–8-point fringe destruction plus beam repair still returns sol_0036, so the failure is not merely single-move locality. Together with sol_0037–0038, this establishes a broad stable basin near n=66: shrinking, swaps, paired toggles, and moderate block repair are exhausted. The remaining plausible weakness is repair bias—beam methods may discard partial masks that become favorable only after many coordinated fringe changes. A global one-sided fringe optimization can test this directly while retaining the successful dense core.
